To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) disparity diversity, reflecting the reputation-based differences among project participants, has a positive impact on market success; (b) separation diversity, measured as the cultural differences among project participants in terms of language and country of residence, has an unexpected positive effect and a negative effect on market success; and (c) variety diversity, reflecting the differences in the roles that participants assume in the projects, has a positive effect on both community engagement and market performance.

(a) disparity diversity, reflecting differences in participants' contribution reputation, is positively related to success; (b) variety diversity, reflecting diversity in project participant roles is positively related to both community engagement and market performance; and (c) separation diversity, reflecting differences among participants in spoken language and country, has an unexpected positive effect of market performance and negative effect on community engagement.

(1) separation and disparity diversity have an unexpected positive impact on market success, (2) variety diversity has an unexpected positive impact, and (3) the impact of variety diversity on market success varies across the project's development stage.
